title: Myth or Fact? Data centres edition

scenes.say: Okay, quick game. Myth, or fact? Data centres edition.
scenes.caption: Okay, quick game. Myth or fact? Data centres edition.

scenes.say: Data centres don't really use water.
scenes.caption: "Data centres don't really use water."

scenes.say: Hmm, no. That's a myth. Servers turn almost all their power into heat, and a lot of data centres use water to cool down. In India, a 2025 study found up to fifty of them in areas with extremely high water stress.
scenes.caption: Hmm, no. That's a myth. Servers turn almost all their power into heat, and many data centres cool down with water. A 2025 study found up to 50 Indian data centres in extremely water-stressed areas.

scenes.say: Okay, but they use most of the world's electricity, right?
scenes.caption: "Okay, but they use most of the world's electricity, right?"

scenes.say: Not quite. It was about one and a half percent in 2024. But here's the thing. The I.E.A. says it could more than double by twenty thirty.
scenes.caption: Not quite. About 1.5% in 2024. But here's the thing: the IEA says it could more than double by 2030.

scenes.say: Fine. But India's power is mostly clean now.
scenes.caption: "Fine. But India's power is mostly clean now."

scenes.say: Half true! Over half of India's power capacity is non-fossil now, which is huge. But coal still makes most of the electricity we actually use.
scenes.caption: Half true! Over half of India's power capacity is non-fossil now. But coal still makes most of the electricity we actually use.

scenes.say: So, the good news? The fixes are real. Cleaner power, smarter cooling, less water. We just have to choose them.
scenes.caption: So, the good news? The fixes are real. Cleaner power, smarter cooling, less water. We just have to choose them.

scenes.caption: Follow The Green Solve

sources: Planet Tracker (2025), as reported by Climate Fact Checks: up to 50 Indian data centres in extremely high water-stress regions
IEA, Energy and AI (2025): data centres ~1.5% of global electricity in 2024; ~945 TWh projected by 2030
MNRE: non-fossil sources over 54% of installed capacity (31 July 2026)
